With these words, Vaidehi circumambulated the pyre and

And a great multitude were assembled there, amongst which

That fortunate princess 
entering the fire, which is nourished by oblations, seemed, in the

Then all the women cried out :-'Alas I ' on seeing her, like

Lifting up their great arms and bands adorned with jewels, 
they made obeisance with joined palms and the King of the Gods 
addressing Ragbava, said :-
" 0 Creator of the Universe and foremost of those versed in 
the spiritual science, how canst thou manifest indifference to 
Sita falling into the &ames ? How art thou unaware that thou 
thyself art the Chief of the Gods ? Formerly thou wert the 
Vasu Ritadhaman, the Progenitor of the Vasus I Thou art the 
Creator of the Three Worlds, Swyamprabhu, the eighth Rudra 
and the fifth of the Sadhyas. The Twin Ashwins are thy twO 
ears, the sun and moon thine eyes ; these are the forms at the 
beginning, middle and end of creation in which thou dost 
appear, 0 Scourge of Thy Foes; and yet thou dost distrUSt 
Vaidehi as if thou wert an ordinary man I " 
Thus addressed by the Protector of the Worlds, the Leader of 
the Gods, Raghava, Lord of Peoples, Foremost of the Pious, 
answered:-
" I deem myself to be a man, Rama, hom of Dasaratha ; 
who then am I in reality ? From whence have I come ? Let 
the Grandsire of the World inform me ! " 
Thus spoke Kakutstha and Brahms, foremost of those who 
know the truth, addressed him saying :-
" Thou art the great and effulgent God Narayana, the 
fortunate Lord armed with the discus. Thou art the One-
Tusked Boar, the Conqueror of thy Foes in the past and the 
future. Thou art the imperishable Brahman, Existence Itself, 
transcending the three divisions of time ; Thou art the Law of 
Righteousneas, the Four-armed, the Bearer of the Shamga Bow ; 
Thou art the Subduer of the senses, the Supreme Purusha ; 
Thou art invincible, Thou art the Holder of the Dagger, Thou 
art Vishnu, Thou art Krishna and of immeasurable might ; 
Thou art Senani and Gramani, the Controller of passions, the 
Origin and Dissolution ; Thou art Upendra and the Slayer of

brief.summary_1line: After Sita enters the fire, the gods arrive and Brahma reveals that Rama is the divine Vishnu incarnate who came to slay Ravana.

image_candidates.scene_text: Sita, calm and resolute, steps into the blazing sacrificial fire before a vast crowd of monkeys, warriors, and weeping women.
The sky fills with radiant chariots as Brahma, Shiva, Indra, and other gods descend above Lanka to address Rama.
Brahma stands before Rama and proclaims his divine nature as Vishnu while the assembled gods bow with folded hands.

deep.rich_summary: Sita, declaring her unwavering fidelity to Rama and calling upon the cosmic Witness, enters the blazing fire to prove her purity before the assembled armies, sages, gods, and common people. The crowd erupts in grief as she vanishes into the flames like a sacred offering. As Rama stands sorrowful, the greatest gods—Indra, Yama, Varuna, Mahadeva, and Brahma—arrive in radiant chariots. They rebuke Rama for acting as though he were merely human and reveal his true identity. At Rama’s own request for clarity, Brahma proclaims the cosmic truth: Rama is none other than Narayana/Vishnu, the eternal Supreme Being who incarnated to destroy Ravana. Sita is Lakshmi herself. With Ravana slain, the divine mission is complete. The scene transforms the epic from heroic war story into cosmic revelation, declaring Rama’s divine nature and the theological meaning of his incarnation.

highlight_spans.why: Sita’s solemn vow of purity and her fearless entry into the fire—one of the Ramayana’s most emotionally charged and controversial moments.
The crowd’s horrified reaction and the sacrificial imagery portraying Sita as a sacred offering, reinforcing ritual and cosmic symbolism.
The dramatic arrival of the assembled gods in radiant chariots at Lanka, marking the shift from human drama to divine revelation.
Brahma’s proclamation revealing Rama as Narayana/Vishnu, listing his cosmic forms and declaring the divine purpose of his incarnation.

top_scenes.scene_text: Sita, serene and radiant, walks into a towering sacrificial fire before a vast crowd of monkeys, warriors, sages, and weeping women as flames rise like a ritual altar.
The sky above Lanka fills with blazing celestial chariots as Brahma, Shiva, Indra, and other gods descend in radiant splendor to address Rama.
Brahma standing before Rama on the battlefield, proclaiming his cosmic identity while the universe—sun, moon, mountains, and stars—seems symbolically reflected around him.
